data.title: Commit for Good | AI × Open Source × Public Good
data.details:
COMMIT FOR GOOD is a three-day hackathon focused on building open-source AI solutions for real-world public-good challenges.

The Hackathon is being organized under the Indo-Swiss Research Grant, with ETH Zurich, University of Lausanne, Indian Institute of Information Technology Allahabad (IIIT Allahabad), and Manipal University Jaipur (MUJ) as participating research institutions, alongside Techideate Qureka, Directorate of Student’s Welfare (DSW), Department of Information Technology, and WikiClub Tech. The event brings together students, researchers and collaborators to encourage innovation at the intersection of AI, open source and public good.

Participants will explore broad challenge domains, identify real-world problems that deserve to be solved, research and validate those problems, and develop innovative AI-driven solutions. The hackathon emphasizes original thinking, practical implementation, collaboration, open-source development and social impact.

Eligibility:

  • Open to college students from recognized institutions.
  • Students from any discipline can participate.
  • Inter-college teams are allowed.
  • Inter-specialization/inter-department teams are allowed.
  • Students from Manipal University Jaipur and other institutions can participate.

Team Formation:

  • Participation is in teams of 1–3 members.
  • Team members may belong to different colleges, universities or academic disciplines.
  • Each participant can be a member of only one team.

What is COMMIT FOR GOOD?

COMMIT FOR GOOD challenges participants to go beyond simply solving a predefined problem.

Teams will be given a broad problem domain or challenge theme and will be expected to independently explore it, identify a meaningful and well-defined problem, understand who is affected and why the problem matters, and investigate existing approaches before proposing their own solution.

The hackathon progresses from problem discovery and validation to solution development, prototyping and open-source release. Participants are encouraged to explore overlooked problems, challenge existing approaches and develop AI-powered solutions with meaningful public impact.

Event Format:

The hackathon follows a hybrid format, combining offline and online phases for problem discovery, development, mentoring, evaluation and the grand finale.

The event consists of:

  • Day 1 – DISCOVER: Explore the given challenge domain, identify and validate a real-world problem, and propose an innovative solution.
  • Day 2 – BUILD: Develop the proposed solution into a detailed solution and working prototype, with mentoring and evaluation.
  • Day 3 – COMMIT: Finalize the solution, present the prototype and showcase the final open-source contribution.

Detailed requirements and submission guidelines for each round will be provided in the respective round sections.

Evaluation Criteria:

Teams will be evaluated on:

  • Problem Discovery & Significance
  • Originality and Innovation
  • Problem Validation and Research
  • Solution Quality and Feasibility
  • Effective Application of AI
  • Practical Applicability and Potential Impact
  • Quality of Prototype and Technical Implementation
  • Final Presentation and Demonstration

Rules:

  • All submissions must be original work created by the participating team.
  • Teams must independently identify and define the problem they wish to address within the given challenge domain.
  • Any sources, datasets, research or existing solutions used by the team should be appropriately acknowledged.
  • The use of AI tools is permitted; teams may use tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other AI systems during the hackathon.
  • Teams may be required to disclose how AI tools were used during the development of their solution.
  • Teams must adhere to all submission deadlines and competition guidelines.
  • Participants are expected to maintain meaningful contributions to their team's work.
  • Organizers reserve the right to modify timelines, evaluation procedures or event details if required.
  • The decision of the jury and organizing committee will be final and binding.

Registration Fee:

  • Registration Fee: Nil
  • The hackathon is free for all participants.

Prizes:

Total Prize Pool: ₹20,000

  • First Prize: ₹10,000
  • Second Prize: ₹6,000
  • Third Prize: ₹4,000

Opportunities:

  • Explore and identify real-world problems within a broad public-good challenge domain.
  • Develop solutions to problems that you discover and define yourself.
  • Receive mentorship and feedback from experts.
  • Collaborate with participants from different disciplines and institutions.
  • Build and showcase a functional AI prototype.
  • Develop solutions with potential for further open-source development.
  • Network with researchers, academics and industry professionals.
  • Get an opportunity to take an idea from problem discovery to a working solution.

Important Links

  • Join the Official WhatsApp Community:https://chat.whatsapp.com/Dg8oXTQDiH8JqPhQQpJpt8

data.title: Hacktoberfest × BFIT 2026
data.details:
A two-day, on-campus tech festival of hackathons, hands-on workshops and speaker sessions, open to every student, tech and non-tech alike.

Event Details

  • Dates: 24-25 October 2026 (Saturday and Sunday)
  • Mode: Offline, both days in person
  • Venue: BFIT Campus, Dehradun, Uttarakhand

About the event

Hacktoberfest × BFIT 2026 is a two-day tech event hosted by BFIT Group of Institutions, Dehradun. It brings students, mentors and industry speakers into one room to learn, build and ship together. The event is for everyone. Whether you write code every day or have never opened a terminal, there is a place for you in a workshop, on a hackathon team, or in the audience of a talk.

What happens

  • Workshops: practical, hands-on sessions, from developer tools and AI to design, product and the creative side of tech.
  • Hackathon: teams start in an online round with mentors. Teams that qualify go to the offline finale on campus, where they build, demo and compete for prizes.
  • Speaker sessions: talks, fireside chats and Q&As with founders, engineers and creators sharing real industry experience.

How the hackathon works

  • Online round: teams register and work on their ideas online, with guidance from mentors.
  • Qualification: teams that clear the online round are invited to join offline.
  • Offline finale: qualified teams build, demo and compete on campus on 24-25 October.

Online round dates will be announced with registrations.

Team size

1-4 members per team. You can take part solo or bring up to three teammates.

Who can participate

  • Tech students: CS, IT and engineering students who want to build, compete and sharpen their skills.
  • Non-tech students: students from management, design, law, health sciences and other fields who want to learn, pitch and collaborate.

Prizes and perks

  • Prizes for the top 10 teams
  • Swag kits for every member of the top 10 teams and for all mentors
  • Certificates of participation for every participant
  • $50+ in free credits across different platforms, for every participant
  • 3 months of ElevenLabs Premium for everyone in the hackathons and workshops

Register now and be part of the festival!

data.title: Game Vita 5.0 - Worst Game Wins
data.details:
Theme-Steampunk

 

The Worst Game Wins | 2-Day Online Game Jam

Make the worst game possible. Win by being the best at it.

Most game jams reward polish, balance, and great design. This one rewards the opposite, with one catch: your terrible game must still be a complete, playable, fully committed piece of work.

About the Event

The Worst Game Wins is a 2-day online game jam where teams intentionally build the worst possible game around a given theme. Think clunky mechanics, absurd controls, nonsensical rules, and gloriously awful UX, all executed with total commitment to the bit.

This is not a "do nothing" event. Bad design is the goal, but low effort is not. Judges are looking for teams who put real craft into making something deliberately terrible.

The Challenge

On Day 1, teams receive a theme that their game must clearly implement. From there, you have two days to design, build, test, and polish your masterpiece of awfulness, then submit it for judging.

Minimum Requirements

To qualify, every submission must:

  • Be playable start to finish: no crashes, no placeholder or empty builds
  • Clearly implement the theme: the theme must be identifiable in the game
  • Include at least one core mechanic
  • Have a win/lose condition
  • Have basic UI: a menu and/or instructions screen

️ "Bad" must be deliberate. Missing features or broken builds are not a substitute for bad design. Intentional badness is the whole point, and it will be judged.

Judging Criteria

Entries will be evaluated on:

  • Hilarity: Does it make people laugh (or rage)?
  • Creativity: How original and inventive is the badness?
  • Intentional Bad Design: Is the awfulness clearly deliberate and well executed?
  • Thematic Relevance: How well does the game reflect the given theme?
  • Commitment to the Bit: How fully did the team go all in on the "worst game" concept, while still delivering a complete, playable game?

Prizes

Total prize pool: ₹2,500

Prize distribution among the top teams will be announced by the organizers.

️ Event Details

Format Online
Duration 2 Days
Dates October 10–11
Team Size 1-4 members

Who Should Participate?

  • Game developers, designers, artists, and writers
  • Beginners looking for a low-pressure way to build their first game
  • Experienced devs who want to flex their creativity (and sense of humor)
  • Anyone who has ever said, "I could make a worse game than this"

You can use any game engine or tool (Unity, Godot, Unreal, GameMaker, Scratch, web-based, etc.).

Submission Guidelines

Submit a Google Drive link to a single .zip file containing the following:

  1. Complete Game Build: A fully playable game that runs from start to finish without crashes. Include all necessary files required to run the game, along with brief instructions if the setup is not self-explanatory.

  2. README File (README.txt or README.md): Include the following information:

    • Game Name and Team Name: The title of your game and the name of your team.

    • Game Description: A brief overview of your game and its core gameplay.

    • Theme Implementation: An explanation of how your game incorporates the given theme.

    • Intentional Bad Design Choices: A description of the deliberately poor design choices you made and how they contribute to the game's concept.

  3. Gameplay Video: A 3–5 minute recording demonstrating your game, starting from the main menu and continuing through to a win or lose ending. This video will allow the judges to experience your game even if they encounter issues running the build. Submit the video in a commonly supported format, such as .mp4.

Important: Ensure that all the required files are included in the ZIP archive and that the Google Drive link provides access to the complete submission.

Make sure the zip opens cleanly and the game runs as described. Submit before the deadline at the end of Day 2.

data.title: Hackathon: Qiskit Fall Fest x IIIT Delhi
data.details:
Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 x IIIT Delhi

One Week. One Quantum Journey. Endless Possibilities.

About the Event:

  • Quantica, under CQT at IIIT Delhi, presents Qiskit Fall Fest 2026; a week-long celebration of quantum computing featuring a beginner-friendly learning track, an online quantum hackathon, and an in-person quantum research showcase.
  • Whether you're taking your first steps into quantum computing or already working on quantum research and applications, this festival gives you the opportunity to learn, build, experiment, and showcase your work.
  • Total Prize Pool: ₹35,000
  • Participation: Free
  • Event Dates: 9–16 October 2026
  • IIIT Delhi + Online

What's Happening?

The festival brings together four major experiences.

1. Quantum & Qiskit 101:
New to quantum computing? Start here! Join a beginner-friendly introduction to Qiskit and quantum computing, with hands-on learning and an opportunity to run programs on a real IBM quantum computer. No prior quantum computing experience is required. Learn the fundamentals of quantum computing. Get hands-on experience with Qiskit. Run your first quantum program. Explore quantum computing through practical examples. Prepare for the hackathon

2. The Quantum Hackathon:
BUILD • EXPERIMENT • SOLVE Teams of 2–4 participants will choose one of three quantum computing tracks. Each track comes with a ready-made tutorial and challenges designed for different experience levels, making the hackathon accessible to participants with varying levels of quantum computing experience.

Track 1: Quantum Chemistry: From Bonds to Qubits. Explore how a molecule's energy changes as its bond stretches, and then tackle the same problem using fewer quantum resources.

Track 2: Quantum Optimization: Smarter Choices at Scale. Use a quantum optimization algorithm to choose the best set of stocks, then scale the problem up.

Track 3: Quantum Simulation: Dynamics Under Noise Simulate the time evolution of a chain of tiny magnets, then correct for noise on real quantum hardware.

3. Qiskit Quest (Solo Beginner Track):
LEARN AT YOUR OWN PACE • GET CERTIFIED. Prefer to work individually? Qiskit Quest is a guided, self-paced track designed for solo participants and beginners who want to build quantum skills without joining a hackathon team. Complete self-paced, auto-graded learning modules. Master quantum fundamentals at your own speed. No prior experience needed. Earn an official certificate of completion

4. Research Poster Showcase:
PRESENT • NETWORK • WIN
Open to individual students and researchers looking to present their work in quantum or quantum-adjacent fields. Showcase your project, connect with peers, and compete for prizes during our hybrid finale. Present quantum projects or research to faculty and industry judges. Participate individually or in research teams. Compete for both Judged and People's Choice awards. Abstract submission deadline: October 12

Abstract Submission:

  • Deadline: Monday, 12th October
    Submission Link: https://forms.gle/rgKxqRfH7mL6qLVg6 (Click Here)

Poster Showcase:

  • 16 October
  • 2:00 PM – 6:00 PM
  • IIIT Delhi

Awards:

  • Judged Prize: Recognizing outstanding quantum research.
  • People's Choice: An audience-selected favorite.

Event Timeline:

9 OCT - Quantum & Qiskit 101:

  • Friday | 2:00–4:00 PM | Online
  • Hands-on Qiskit introduction + real IBM quantum computer run + hackathon briefing.

10 OCT - Hackathon Kickoff:

  • Saturday | 10:00 AM | Online
  • Challenges released and tutorials begin.

11–14 OCT - Build & Explore:

  • Online
  • Work on your chosen hackathon challenge, experiment with quantum computing, and develop your solution.
  • Hackathon submission closes: 14 October, midnight

15 OCT - Judging Day (Online):

  • Judges evaluate the submitted hackathon solutions and select the finalists.

16 OCT - The Finale:

  • Friday | 2:00–6:00 PM | In Person (Offline) | IIIT Delhi
  • Research poster showcase
  • Hackathon finalist presentations
  • One team per track
  • Awards & finale

New to Quantum?

  • Don't worry!
  • Participants who are new to quantum computing can explore Qiskit Quest - the Beginner Track, featuring self-paced, auto-graded modules designed for beginners.
  • Complete the set of paths and earn a certificate while building your quantum computing fundamentals.

Why Participate?

Ready to Enter the Quantum World?

data.title: Robo Race
data.details:
Rules:

  • Robot Specifications: The robot must meet the prescribed dimensions, weight, and power requirements, with a focus on reliable drive systems, robust construction, and effective control.
  • Race Regulations: Robots compete on a designated track featuring turns, obstacles, ramps, and other challenges. Teams must complete the course within the stipulated time while staying within the track boundaries.
  • Safety Compliance: All robots must pass a mandatory safety inspection. Components must be securely mounted, batteries properly protected, and the robot must have a safe and reliable power-control mechanism.

Format:

  • Team Composition: Each team can have a maximum of six participants and must register through the official website.
  • Competition Stages: Teams first compete in qualifying rounds, where they race against the clock or other participants. Top-performing teams advance to subsequent rounds, leading to the final race.
  • Judging Criteria: Rankings are determined primarily by completion time, with penalties added for violations such as missing checkpoints, leaving the track, or failing to clear designated obstacles. In case of a tie, additional factors such as penalty count and a tie-breaker race may be used.

data.title: Drone Soccer
data.details:
Rules & Guidelines:

  • Team Structure:
    • Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 5 members.
    • Cross-college teams are allowed—participants from different institutions can team up.
  • Model Regulations:
    • Each team must use its own custom-built or custom-configured drone wrapped in a protective cage/exoskeleton; exchanging models or components between teams during match rounds is strictly prohibited.
    • Standard RTF (Ready-To-Fly) commercial consumer drones are not allowed, though pre-programmed flight controllers and stabilization boards are permitted.
    • Only one main drone model can be used throughout all competition rounds.
  • Flight and Conduct Rules:
    • No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams will receive a 2-minute warm-up/trial period before Round 2 matches.
    • Lifting or repositioning the drone manually during active gameplay is strictly prohibited.
    • A drone that crashes and is unable to take off within the allotted restart window immediately forfeits that specific attempt or round.
    • The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on all match rules, scoring disputes, and safety calls.

Event Structure:

Round 1: Drone Soccer Arena Showdown:

  • Obstacle & Defender Navigation: Teams must pilot their caged drones through an active arena featuring physical obstacles and designated opponent defense zones.
  • Goal Scoring Task:
    • Teams must navigate their drone past defensive barricades and maneuver it cleanly through the elevated circular Goal Ring to score points.
    • Each successful goal scored within the match time earns points based on precision and execution.
    • If a goal attempt fails, misses, or bounces off the goal frame, no points are awarded, but no negative penalty is incurred. Teams can immediately reset and attempt another run.
  • Match Execution: Matches are conducted in timed sprints where agility, mid-air defense, collision recovery, and scoring accuracy determine the final winners.

data.title: QCTF – Quantum Capture the Flag
data.details:
QCTF – Quantum Capture the Flag

Event Description:

QCTF – Quantum Capture the Flag is a technical, team-based competition that combines the challenge-driven format of Capture the Flag (CTF) with concepts from quantum computing, programming, cryptography, and logical problem-solving.

Teams will receive a collection of challenges requiring them to analyze information, solve technical problems, interpret quantum concepts, decode clues, debug code, or complete computational tasks to uncover and submit hidden flags. Depending on the final challenge design, problems may involve quantum circuits, Qiskit programming, probability, quantum information, cryptography, logic, debugging, data interpretation, and other related areas.

The event begins with a Qualification CTF, designed to assess participants' problem-solving abilities and determine the teams that advance to the final challenge. Shortlisted teams will then compete in the main CTF, which will feature clearly defined challenges, point values, submission requirements, time limits, and a flag-verification mechanism.

Teams can divide challenges among members based on their individual strengths, making communication, collaboration, and efficient problem-solving important aspects of the competition.

Scoring will primarily be based on verified flags and the published point values of the challenges. Time may be used as a tie-breaker where specified in advance. The event is designed for participants looking for a technical and challenge-oriented introduction to quantum computing and related problem-solving techniques.

Duration:

  • Round 1: Qualification CTF
  • Round 2: Final Quantum CTF

The exact duration, challenge count, qualification criteria, and schedule for each round will be communicated by the organizers.

Rules & Guidelines:

  • Participation is team-based. The final team-size limit will be specified by the organizers.
  • Participants should have familiarity with relevant areas such as Python/Qiskit, quantum computing basics, problem-solving, cryptography, and logical reasoning.
  • The competition will begin with a Qualification CTF to determine the teams advancing to the final challenge.
  • The final CTF will consist of multiple technical challenges with clearly defined point values, submission requirements, and time limits.
  • Teams must solve challenges and submit the corresponding flags through the designated submission mechanism.
  • Only verified flags will be counted toward the team's score.
  • Challenge points will be awarded according to the published scoring system.
  • Time may be considered as a tie-breaker only when specified by the organizers before the competition.
  • Teams may divide challenges among members and collaborate internally to solve problems.
  • Teams must not share flags, solutions, or challenge-specific information with other competing teams during the competition.
  • Participants may use only the tools, programming languages, libraries, references, and other resources explicitly permitted by the organizers.
  • Any external resources or tools used must comply with the rules announced for the specific challenge.
  • Exploiting unintended vulnerabilities in the competition infrastructure, interfering with other teams, attacking competition systems outside the permitted challenge environment, or otherwise attempting to compromise the event infrastructure is prohibited.
  • Plagiarism, flag sharing, unauthorized collaboration, or any form of unfair assistance may result in disqualification.
  • Teams must follow all challenge-specific instructions, submission formats, and deadlines.
  • In case of technical issues or disputes, participants must immediately report them to the organizing team rather than attempting unauthorized workarounds.
  • The organizers may modify challenge availability or procedures when necessary to maintain fair competition.
  • The decisions of the organizing and judging team regarding challenge validation, scoring, qualification, and final results will be final.

data.title: Hardware Session – Circuit Optimization Challenge
data.details:
Description

  • Circuit Optimization Challenge is a hands-on quantum computing competition focused on improving the efficiency of quantum circuits. Participants will receive one or more quantum circuits and will be asked to optimize them while preserving the required computational behaviour or output.
  • The challenge may involve reducing unnecessary gates, lowering circuit depth, improving gate usage, simplifying equivalent operations, and considering practical hardware constraints. Participants are expected to work with concepts such as quantum gates, circuit depth, qubit operations and Qiskit-based circuit construction.
  • The event tests whether participants can move beyond simply writing a circuit and instead reason about how a circuit can be made more efficient and execution-friendly. A short qualifier or sample optimization task can be used to verify readiness before the main challenge. Evaluation can consider correctness, degree of optimization, resource usage, technical reasoning and compliance with stated constraints.
  • The challenge is suitable for participants who have basic exposure to quantum circuits and Python/Qiskit and want to apply those concepts in a practical setting.

Duration

  • Total Duration: 90–120 minutes

Rules & Guidelines

  • Participants must compete individually.
  • Participants will be provided with one or more quantum circuits for optimization.
  • The optimized circuit must preserve the required computational behaviour or specified output.
  • Participants may reduce unnecessary gates, circuit depth, qubit operations, or other specified resource usage.
  • Python and Qiskit may be used for circuit construction, analysis, simulation, and optimization.
  • Participants must follow any gate, qubit, depth, or hardware constraints specified by the organizers.
  • Solutions should be submitted within the allotted time.
  • Participants may be required to provide the optimized circuit along with a brief explanation of the changes made.
  • Evaluation may consider correctness, circuit optimization, resource usage, technical reasoning, and compliance with constraints.
  • Plagiarism, copying another participant's solution, or using unauthorized external assistance is not permitted.
  • The organizer's decision regarding evaluation and final results will be considered final.
  • Exact submission format, allowed software/libraries, hardware restrictions, scoring method, and other event-specific rules should be announced before the competition.

data.title: HackRobo 2.0
data.details:
Overview:

HACKROBO 2.0 is a 2-day national hardware hackathon that challenges undergraduate engineering students to design, build, and demonstrate innovative robotic solutions for a real-world environmental challenge. The 2026–27 edition focuses on Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots, with participants working on solutions that can operate in open water while reaching and retrieving debris accumulated along riverbanks.

The hackathon encourages teams to combine mechanical design, electronics, embedded systems, robotics, and software to develop a functional prototype addressing the given problem statement.

  • Date: 10–11 October 2026
  • No. of Days: 2 Days
  • Duration: 36 Hours
  • Members Count: 3–5 per team
  • Eligibility: Undergraduate Engineering Students
  • Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed
  • Mode: Offline
  • Registration Fees: ₹2,000 per team
  • Venue: Pillai College of Engineering, New Panvel East, Navi Mumbai

Theme / Domain: Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots

The hackathon focuses on developing robotic solutions for riverbank and river cleaning.

Conventional aquatic cleanup systems primarily target floating waste in open water, while significant amounts of plastic and other debris accumulate along muddy riverbanks above the waterline. These areas can be difficult to access using conventional cleanup vessels.

Participants are challenged to:

Design a robot that can move through open water and reach riverbank debris without getting stuck.

Teams are encouraged to explore solutions involving autonomous navigation, manual control, robotic manipulation, buoyancy, waterproofing, and stable operation near challenging shoreline conditions.

Suggested Technical Approach

Teams may explore a hybrid Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) incorporating:

  • Dual-Mode Control: Autonomous GPS/waypoint navigation for open water with manual RC override near the shoreline.
  • Articulated Arm: A 2–4 DoF robotic arm capable of retrieving debris without grounding the vessel.
  • Power & Buoyancy: A stable and waterproof vessel capable of maintaining stability even when the arm is fully extended.
  • Integrated Systems: Combination of mechanical, electronic, embedded, and software systems to achieve the required functionality.

Event Format

The event will be conducted over 24 hours across two days.

  • Day 1: Registration, orientation, opening ceremony, hackathon commencement, mentoring, networking and jamming session.
  • Day 2: Mentoring, final project submission, judging and winner announcement.
  • Teams will work continuously on their prototypes during the hackathon.
  • Mentors and volunteers will be available to provide technical guidance throughout the event.
  • The detailed schedule is tentative and may be modified by the organizers.

Judging

Projects will be evaluated based on:

  • Innovation
  • Functionality
  • Impact
  • Presentation
  • Working prototype/demonstration

A functional working prototype is strongly encouraged for the final evaluation.

Facilities & Perks

  • On-campus accommodation
  • Meals throughout the event
  • Workspace access
  • Mentorship from industry experts
  • Networking opportunities
  • Participation certificates
  • Winner recognition
  • Industry exposure
  • Opportunity to build a real hardware prototype

Rules & Guidelines:

  • Teams must consist of 3 to 5 members.
  • Inter-specialization teams are allowed, provided all members are undergraduate engineering students from the same institution.
  • Participants must work on the designated Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots domain.
  • Teams are expected to develop and demonstrate a functional robotic solution to the given problem statement.
  • Teams must complete and submit their project within the specified hackathon timeline.
  • Teams must follow all instructions provided by the organizers and mentors.
  • Only approved resources may be used during the hackathon.
  • Participants must maintain fair play, discipline, and professional conduct throughout the event.
  • Teams must be available for mentoring and evaluation rounds as scheduled.
  • The final project must be submitted before the final judging round.
  • Judges may evaluate the project based on innovation, functionality, impact, and presentation.
  • Any violation of the event guidelines or engagement in unfair practices may result in disqualification.
  • The event schedule is tentative and may be modified by the organizers if required.
  • Decisions made by the organizing and judging committee regarding the competition will be considered final.

Prize Pool:

₹75,000

The prize pool will be distributed among the top-performing teams, along with possible special recognition awards.

Why Participate?

  • Build a real-world hardware solution
  • Gain hands-on experience in robotics and engineering
  • Work on an environmental challenge
  • Receive mentorship and technical guidance
  • Network with students, mentors, and professionals
  • Gain industry exposure
  • Strengthen your engineering portfolio
  • Earn certificates and recognition
  • Experience an intensive 24-hour hardware hackathon

HACKROBO 2.0 is an opportunity to move beyond ideas and build, test, and demonstrate a real robotic solution to a real-world problem.

data.details:
Event Details

  • Date: 24 October 2026
  • Time: 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM
  • Venue: NewGen IEDC FAB LAB, I.T.S Engineering College, Greater Noida
  • Registration Fee: ₹300 per team
  • Prize Pool: ₹12,000
  • Team Size: 3 participants per team
  • Coordinator: Mr. Deepak Kumar

Event Description

Make-A-Thon is a sustainability-focused "Best Out of Waste" challenge that puts participants' engineering creativity and resourcefulness to the test. Using only scrap materials provided by the organizers, teams must transform waste into something useful or innovative — belonging to any category (civil, mechanical, electrical, artistic, or otherwise) — tackling the problem of modern-day waste generation through practical, sustainable innovation.

Guidelines

Eligibility & Team Composition

  • Team Size: Maximum 3 participants per team
  • Open to undergraduate/postgraduate students and eligible participants from colleges/institutions
  • Valid institutional ID is mandatory
  • Both team members must work collaboratively to build the item within the given time

Material Usage & Constraints

  • Only scrap materials provided by the organizers may be used, and must be repurposed into the final creation
  • Decorative or custom-made materials brought solely for aesthetic enhancement (paints, stickers, or any external items) are strictly prohibited

Tools & Equipment

  • Participants must bring their own basic construction tools (adhesives, tapes, scissors, cutting tools)
  • Limited light workshop tools and safety equipment may be available at the venue, but teams should not rely on this
  • Any provided workshop tool must be used with appropriate safety equipment and only under the direct supervision of an event coordinator

Time Limit

  • Teams have exactly 1 hour to complete their project
  • A warning bell rings at the 45-minute mark, signalling 15 minutes remaining
  • Work must stop immediately once time expires; going over time may result in point deductions or disqualification

Presentation
After time is up, teams must present their creation to the judges, explaining:

  • Purpose — what the item is and how it can be used
  • Concept — the idea and thought process behind its design
  • Usefulness — its practical application and utility

Rules

  • Work may begin only after the official start signal
  • No participant may receive assistance from anyone outside their registered team
  • Teams are expected to develop their own solutions; plagiarism or use of unauthorized external work may lead to disqualification

Judging Criteria

Entries are evaluated on:

  • Creativity & Innovation — how uniquely the scrap materials have been used to create something novel and useful
  • Functionality — whether the item actually serves a practical, useful purpose
  • Presentation & Explanation — clarity and depth of the team's explanation of their concept
  • Resourcefulness — the team's ability to work effectively within the constraint of only using provided scrap materials and basic tools

Disqualification

A team may be disqualified for:

  • Using materials other than the organizer-provided scrap (e.g., aesthetic add-ons)
  • Continuing work after the time limit expires
  • Receiving outside assistance during the build
  • Plagiarism or use of unauthorized pre-existing work
  • Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, unsportsmanlike conduct, or failure to follow safety guidelines
  • Failure to follow general tool-safety protocols while using workshop tools

The judge's decision regarding final scores and any rule violations is final and binding.

Opportunities for Participants

  • Win credential sponsorship worth up to ₹15,00,000.
  • Also you will get Incubation Support of 90k.
  • Receive event certificates through TruScholar’s blockchain-powered digital credential platform.

  • Lifetime access to the TruScholar Smart Credential Wallet.
  • AI-powered Career Coach.

  • TruResume – ATS-friendly AI Resume Builder.
  • Integrated Job & Internship Portal.

Tools & Equipment:

  • Participants must bring their own basic construction tools (adhesives, tapes, scissors, and cutting tools).
  • Limited light workshop tools and safety equipment may be available at the venue, but teams should not rely on this.
  • Any provided workshop tool must be used with appropriate safety equipment and only under the direct supervision of an event coordinator.

Time Limit:

  • Suggested working duration: 90 minutes; the final duration will be confirmed and announced before the round begins.
  • Work begins only after the official start signal and must stop immediately once time expires.

Presentation:

After time is up, teams must present their creation to the judges, explaining:

  • Purpose: What the item is and how it can be used.
  • Concept: The idea and thought process behind its design.
  • Usefulness: Its practical application and utility.

Rules:

  • No participant may receive assistance from anyone outside their registered team.
  • Teams are expected to develop their own solutions; plagiarism or use of unauthorized external work may lead to disqualification.

Judging Criteria:

  • Innovation: 30%
  • Functionality: 30%
  • Resourcefulness: 20%
  • Presentation: 10%
  • Sustainability / Usefulness: 10%

Disqualification:

A team may be disqualified for:

  • Using materials other than the organizer-provided scrap (e.g., aesthetic add-ons).
  • Continuing work after the time limit expires.
  • Receiving outside assistance during the build.
  • Plagiarism or use of unauthorized pre-existing work.
  • Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, unsportsmanlike conduct, or failure to follow safety guidelines.
  • Failure to follow general tool-safety protocols while using workshop tools.

The judge's decision regarding final scores and any rule violations is final and binding.

Note: Registration fees are not refundable.

Organized by Innovation Hacks:

About the Hackathon:

HORIZON X 2K26 is a global AI hackathon where participants build innovative solutions to real-world problems using Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, NLP, RAG, and AI Agents.

Choose ONE of 5 Problem Statements:

  • AI for Disaster Response:
  • Build AI solutions for disaster detection, emergency coordination, damage assessment, or resource allocation.
  • AI for Healthcare:
  • Build responsible AI solutions for healthcare accessibility, workflow automation, information support, or decision assistance.
  • AI for Agriculture:
  • Develop AI solutions for crop disease detection, yield prediction, smart irrigation, pest detection, or farmer assistance.
  • AI for Education:
  • Create AI-powered tutors, personalized learning systems, skill-gap detection, automated feedback, or intelligent assessment tools.
  • AI for Productivity & Automation:
  • Build AI agents or intelligent automation systems that solve real-world workflow and productivity challenges.

Eligibility & Team Format:

  • Open to students, developers, researchers, and technology enthusiasts.
  • Individual or team participation.
    • Team size: 1–4 members.
  • Inter-college teams allowed.
  • Inter-specialization / inter-department teams allowed.
  • Each participant can join only one team.
  • Each team must select one problem statement.

Hackathon Process:

Register → Select Problem → Build → Submit → Judging → Results

Submission Requirements:

  • Project description.
  • GitHub repository.
  • Demo video.
  • Deployment link (if available).

Prizes:

  • 1st Prize — ₹10,000
  • 2nd Prize — ₹6,000
  • 3rd Prize — ₹4,000
  • Total Cash Prize Pool: ₹20,000
  • Winning certificates for winning teams.
  • Winning projects featured on Innovation Hacks social media.
  • Participant certificates for all eligible participants.

Builder Benefits — Breeth:

  • $19 AI Memory Credits

  • Technical Support
  • Winning projects may be eligible for up to $1,000+ worth of Breeth infrastructure credits for 1–3 months to continue development beyond the hackathon and explore startup opportunities.

Breeth credits and extended support are subject to applicable terms, eligibility, and availability.

Judging Criteria:

  • AI / Technical Implementation — 25%.
  • Innovation & Creativity — 20%.
  • Problem-Solution Fit — 20%.
  • Impact & Scalability — 20%.
  • Functionality & Demo — 15%.

Rules:

  • Maximum 4 members per team.
  • Inter-college and inter-specialization teams are allowed.
